title: Composable internal ingress prober + staged TLS adapter Terraform module
creator: Liam Chen
description: Build a reusable Terraform module that composes an internal NLB -> ALB ingress path with configurable TLS termination modes and a pluggable health prober. The module must support staged certificate rotation, per-priority health probes (L7 and TCP), and a weighted fallback mechanism for cross-AZ failover, enabling zero-downtime upgrades for Private (VPC) deployments.
background: Private deployments currently rely on brittle handcrafted stacks for internal ingress. Multiple customers reported brief 5-15s request spikes during certificate rotations and scale-ups. We need a standardized module offering: (1) clear TLS termination choices (NLB passthrough -> ALB terminate, ALB terminate end-to-end), (2) an extensible probe interface so services can supply custom L7 readiness checks, and (3) traffic weighting and sticky-session options for canary/rollouts and cross-AZ failover without manual terraform edits.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published to registry/private-modules with semantic versioning
Module supports two TLS modes: passthrough (NLB TCP) and terminate (ALB TLS) via a single config flag
Pluggable health-prober interface that accepts HTP (HTTP path + headers), TCP ping, or gRPC health check definitions
Certificate rotation flow that follows blue/green key material with autoswitch and no 30s outage observed in canary tests
Configurable weighted target groups with API to set canary weight and automated rollback when health degrades
Cross-AZ connection draining and session affinity options implemented and covered by e2e tests
Documentation with architecture diagram, example consumable module call, and migration notes from older stacks
proposed_solution: Create terraform module 'internal-ingress/composable' with input variables: tls_mode, cert_arn_primary, cert_arn_secondary, probe_definitions, weight_config, stickiness, connection_draining_seconds
Implement two main submodules: nlbalancer (tcp passthrough) and albalancer (listener rules + target group management). Use a single interface to wire backend target groups from private services.

Health prober: provide an AWS Lambda-based synthetic prober (optional) and a native ALB healthcheck configuration generated from 'probe_definitions' variable. Allow custom headers and path, support 200/204 success codes and gRPC status mapping.

Certificate rotation: accept primary+secondary cert ARNs and implement a two-step promotion: attach secondary cert to listener, warm target groups, then switch default action weights and detach old cert after drain.

Weighted fallback: create an Orchestrator object (terraform-managed resource set) that manipulates ALB listener rules and NLB target weights to shift traffic during upgrades or when health falls below threshold.
Add CI step: terraform validate & plan with terratest e2e (localstack for unit, real AWS for integration in staging account).
implementation_notes: Avoid introducing provider-specific workarounds that break Terraform 1.6. Track provider versions in module's required_providers block.
Prefer ALB target group health checks for L7; for raw TCP services use NLB health checks tied to a lightweight sidecar probe endpoint.
Keep IAM scope minimal: module will emit IAM roles only for optional Lambda prober. Document required IAM for operators when Lambda is enabled.
Add feature flag 'enable_synthetic_prober' default false to avoid extra infra for customers not needing it.
Use tags and descriptive names to make debugging and cost allocation easier in customer accounts.
Build a migration script/guide to map old hand-rolled stacks to new module inputs (examples in docs folder).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): implement module skeleton and basic ALB listener + target groups. Unit tests with localstack. (owner: Sana)

Phase 2 (staging): integration tests in dev account with sample microservice, validate connection draining and cert rotation. Run chaos test (terminate ALB/target) and verify automated weighted failover. (owner: eng-infra)
Phase 3 (canary customers): offer module as opt-in for two active Private customers, monitor metrics: request error spikes, latency P95, and cert rotation readiness. (owner: SRE)
Phase 4 (general availability): publish module versioned release, update console docs and templates, and announce migration support.
Rollback: revert to previous listener rule state and weights using saved terraform state snapshot; provide runbook for manual rollback in PVPC accounts.
